chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran, from Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He is questioned in his grave only the one who made faith pure and made disbelief pure; and as for what is besides that, they are distracted from it.
ai.seo_question: Who is questioned in the grave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the grave interrogation (al-Naskh) is strictly for those who were unequivocal in their faith or disbelief, while the 'intermediate' (al-Awsat) are distracted from detailed questioning. This supports the Shia view of a distinct intermediate state for those with mixed beliefs, distinguishing them from the clear-cut believers and disbelievers. The narration emphasizes divine mercy by sparing the ambiguous from rigorous scrutiny.
